reason: E2 shows that a Cr-oxide layer forms on a similar FeCoNiMnCu coating after 800 °C exposure and states it enhances wear resistance, directly supporting the oxide-formation premise. However, the cited evidence does not address pre-oxidation, the role of Cr₂O₃ as a diffusion barrier, or the link between homogeneity and oxide uniformity, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: FeNiCrCoCu forms a protective chromium-oxide layer upon thermal exposure at 800 °C
This oxide layer enhances wear resistance
Pre-oxidation can promote formation of a continuous, adherent Cr₂O₃ layer
The oxide layer acts as a diffusion barrier and reduces metal-to-metal contact
A homogeneous elemental distribution in the coating supports uniform oxide formation
